plotSections.title: The Helm and the Soul Identifier
bullets: The party reviews Carlkin's soul identifier, a small bag resembling a bag of holding; a true phylactery placed inside bursts into flames immediately. The helm only smoldered, so it is not a phylactery.

The smoldering comes from a soul fragment, an echo or remembrance of a soul attached to the helm, which is still strong enough to possess a wearer. Walker likens it to a possessed doll from a B-rated horror film.

Sylan suggests the helm might be one part of a set, with his armor holding the rest of a phylactery. Walker believes phylacteries are single items. Walker was the only one who looted the body, and the keystone is considered an unlikely vessel.
Earlier notes with Carlkin suggested the party had the phylactery with them, so the true phylactery's location remains unknown.
Walker refuses to dispose of or give up the helm. He has already resisted its possession once, considers it unsafe for anyone else, and will wear it himself.

Walker has spoken with the helm's soul once. The party plans to open that channel again after dinner, with Dana supervising, possibly in the large dining room. Mahali urges them to wait until after dinner and wants to watch.

plotSections.title: Evening at Langdale Stronghold
bullets: Araden is too large for the stronghold and lounges at its foot, where Glimmen sits chatting with him among his large collection of books. About a dozen village children have begun gathering near the two dragons.
Mahali serves pork stew and assorted desserts, then retires to the kitchen to prepare breakfast. Gerk's punched potatoes will become a hash for the morning meal.
Ponchi sips from a small gourd flask after the meal, and the guards leave for evening patrols.

chronologicalEvents: Walker recounts that Carlkin's soul identifier showed the helm only smoldering, meaning it holds a soul fragment rather than being a phylactery.
Sylan proposes cutting the soul out with his sword and theorizes that the armor set together forms the phylactery.
The party confirms Walker was the only looter, and the keystone is ruled out.
The DM clarifies that the helm's soul echo can still possess a wearer.
Walker claims the helm and will wear it, having already resisted its possession.
Mahali probes whether the helm could be put on someone else and teases Walker about how it clashes with his gold look, then recommends attempting contact after dinner.
Araden and Glimmen are found at the foot of the stronghold with village children gathered nearby.
Dinner is served, Mahali retires to the kitchen for breakfast prep, and the guards leave on patrol.
The party prepares to attempt communication with the helm.

notes: The helm smoldered in the soul identifier instead of igniting, so it is not a phylactery.
It contains a soul fragment, an echo of a soul, that is capable of possessing a wearer.
Walker has resisted its possession, will wear it himself, and refuses to dispose of it.
Walker has communicated with the soul inside once.
It is white and sterile-looking, unlike Walker's gold armor.
